justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the regex broadening preserves R4-valid strings in R6 and is not an R4-to-R6 base-design break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the R4 regex would improve R6-to-R4 validator compatibility but would preserve older exclusions and narrow the intended R6 lexical space.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local evidence shows `string.value` was broadened from `[ \r\n\t\S]+` to `^[\s\S]+$` while cardinality and max length stayed unchanged. That inferred goal is reasonable for a datatype defined as a sequence of Unicode characters, and the change does not invalidate R4-valid instances in R6. The remaining compatibility cost is reverse-direction: R6 can now permit uncommon characters that R4 validators may reject. Because no official change rationale was available locally, `Probably justified` is more appropriate than an unqualified `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the R6 rule is a widening, not a narrowing. A conservative alternative would have retained the R4 regex and added narrative clarification or warnings, but that would fail the apparent R6 goal of accepting the full non-empty character space described by the datatype. Cross-version guidance remains useful as mitigation for R6-to-R4 conversion, but that is not a less-breaking base R6 design alternative.
